audits.mathematicalReason: Translation preserves orientation. The only possible left-to-right tile adjacencies are II→I, I→IV and IV→III. Using all four tiles in two rows therefore forces the rows to be (II,I) and (IV,III). Placing (II,I) above (IV,III) matches both vertical interfaces: 2=2 in the left column and 7=7 in the right column. Reversing the rows fails because III's bottom label 0 does not match I's top label 8. Thus A=II, B=I, C=IV and D=III. The candidate appropriately treats translation as support; the main deduction is constrained edge matching, which is not covered by the supplied definition.

audits.mathematicalReason: The I, T, X, W, U and V pentominoes have reflection axes. In particular, W and V have diagonal axes, so restricting attention to horizontal and vertical axes would undercount. The other six shapes have no reflection axis. Thus six pentominoes qualify. Checking coincidence under reflection directly assesses the supplied Line Symmetry definition; rotational symmetry alone does not qualify.

audits.mathematicalReason: External tangency gives OP=2+4=6. The radii OA and PD are perpendicular to AD, so they are parallel bases of trapezoid AOPD. Resolving OP parallel and perpendicular to AD gives AD²=6²−(4−2)²=32, hence AD=4√2. The trapezoid's area is (2+4)(4√2)/2=12√2. The lower trapezoid OBCP has the same area, giving 24√2. This validates the candidate's tangent-property and composite-area targets, with circle position, Pythagoras and trapezoid area as supporting knowledge.

audits.mathematicalReason: Write the screen width and height as 4t and 3t. Its diagonal is 5t by the Pythagorean theorem, so t=27/5=5.4 inches. A 2:1 movie filling the screen's width has height 2t. The unused height is therefore 3t−2t=t, divided equally between the two strips. Each strip has height t/2=2.7 inches. The candidate correctly identifies an applied Pythagorean calculation supported by the interpretation of aspect ratios.

routes.label: Four unpainted triangles and square roots
Strip areas, overlap, and completing the square

audits.mathematicalReason: Let the square's side be s and the brush width, measured perpendicular to a stroke, be w. Each unpainted isosceles right triangle has base b=s−√2w and altitude b/2. Their total area is b²=s²/2. Since b>0, b=s/√2, giving s/w=2+2√2. The alternative route is also valid: each clipped strip has area √2sw−w²/2, and their central square overlap has area w². Thus 2√2sw−2w²=s²/2. For r=s/w, completing the square gives (r−2√2)²=4. Only r=2√2+2 satisfies r>√2, the domain in which the four unpainted triangles exist; the smaller root is inadmissible. Both candidate routes are defensible alternatives, not jointly required methods.

figureEvidence.fact: The painted region consists of equal-width bands centered on the two square diagonals, leaving four congruent unpainted triangles with bases on the square's sides.
The stroke boundaries are parallel to the diagonals; the two strokes overlap in a central square.

audits.mathematicalReason: Adding the five segment sums counts every vertex label exactly twice. Their total is therefore 2(3+5+6+7+9)=60. Five arithmetic-sequence terms can be written as m−2d, m−d, m, m+d and m+2d, whose sum is 5m. Consequently m=60/5=12. The conditions are consistent: assigning (A,B,C,D,E)=(3,7,6,5,9) gives segment sums 10,13,11,14,12, which reorder to 10,11,12,13,14. The incidence count and arithmetic-sequence sum both match the supplied assessed scopes.

audits.mathematicalReason: The unit-distance pairs are exactly the eight consecutive boundary pairs: two on each side of the square. There are C(8,2)=28 equally likely unordered pairs, giving probability 8/28=2/7. Alternatively, each first point has exactly two unit-distance neighbors among the seven remaining points, so ordered counting gives (8×2)/(8×7)=2/7. Both candidate counting routes are valid alternatives supporting the equally likely probability target.
